6. The learned Judges noticed the decision of a Single Judge reported in A.I.R. 1958 (Punjab), 47 wherein the learned Single Judge has considered the scope of the proviso and concluded by saying:- 

 7. It was further noticed that in A.I.R. 1962 (Madhya Pradesh), 104 the observation of A.I.R, 1958 (Punjab) was not followed. In that decision in A.I.R. 1962 (Madhya Pradesh) another Single Judge considered that the observation of learned judge in Punjab case was clearly obiter. The view was taken in the Madhya Pradesh case that the function of the proviso was not to restrict the case and expressed "at any time" occurring in the proviso are words of widest amplitude and observed: 

 8. Then the High Court considered the decision reported in A.I.R, 1965 (Rajasthan), 143. In that decision also the learned Judge noticed A.I. R. 1958 (Panjabi) 47. The Rajasthan High Court found it difficult to follow the Punjab ruling and noticed that there is difference between the commencement of the proceedings under section 145 Cr.P.C. and the commencement of the enquiry contemplated by subsection (4). A drawing up of the preliminary order marks the "commencement of the proceedings" under section 145; but stage of the "commencement of the enquiry" is reached only after compile once with sub-section (1) and (2). 

 15. The anxiety of the learned Judge in A.I.R. 1958 (Punjab) was justified because police sent report informing that there was a likelihood of breach of peace on 21-5-66 and the Magistrate himself on 25.5.56 went to the locality and in presence of the parties and their lawyers visited the area and found tension in the area and be considered that the property should be attached and accordingly asked the parties to argue the matter on 25-5-56. On that date (25.5.56) the Magistrate passed after bearing the argument the order of attachment without drawing up the order under sub-section (1). That has been taken exception by Tekchand, J. and an argument was advanced questioning power of passing such an order and in considering that argument the observation was made in obiter. Hence the decision in A. I. R. 1958 (Punjab), 47 is no authority for the purpose to say that a Magistrate has no power to pass an order of attachment unless stage as contemplated in subsection (3) is reached. We have not come across any decision from any other jurisdiction of this subcontinent where such view as has been expressed in A. I. R. 1958 (Punjab) 47 was followed. Nor the learned Advocate could cite any other single decision where such view was followed. 

 24. In the 26 D.L.R. 291 case, the cases reported in A.I.R. 1958 (Punjab) 47, A.I.R. 1962 (Madhya Pradesh,) 104 and A.I.R 1965 Rajasthan, 143 were considered and view taken in A.I.R. 1958 (Punjab), 47 case was accepted, and those given in other two cases were not accepted for the reasons elaborately discussed in the said case reported in 26 D.L.R. 291.
